name: oxabl
description: Progress ABL for VS Code: syntax highlighting, plus format-on-save and live diagnostics from the oxabl language server, driven from oxabl.toml.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Building runs the worker command from oxabl.toml, so no build runs in an untrusted workspace. Highlighting, formatting and diagnostics still work. The settings that name a program or its arguments are not read until you trust the workspace.

commands.title: oxabl: Install or Update the CLI

oxabl.enable.description: Enable the oxabl language server (format-on-save and diagnostics). Applied automatically when changed; no window reload needed.

oxabl.server.path.description: Absolute path to the `oxabl` executable. When empty, the extension uses `~/.local/bin/oxabl` (or `$OXABL_INSTALL_DIR/oxabl`), then `oxabl` from your PATH.

enumDescriptions: Check GitHub Releases once a day, then download, verify and install a newer version. Acts as "notify" when VS Code's `extensions.autoUpdate` is false.
Check once a day and ask before installing a newer version.
Never check by itself. The `oxabl: Check for Updates` command still works.
oxabl.updates.description: How the extension updates itself from GitHub Releases. It is not on the Marketplace, so VS Code does not update it.

oxabl.trace.server.description: Trace the JSON-RPC communication between VS Code and the oxabl language server (for debugging).

oxabl.build.enable.description: Build the project with `oxabl build` when it opens and when a file changes. Applied automatically when changed. The commands `oxabl: Build` and `oxabl: Cancel Build` work in either case.

oxabl.build.debounce.description: Milliseconds to wait after the last change before a build starts. A build starts at the latest 5 seconds after the first change.

oxabl.build.args.description: Extra arguments for `oxabl build`, for example `["--config-overlay", "/path/overlay.toml"]`. Also passed when the extension reads the build setup of a project.
